item.title: Parliament to vote in December on proposed pesticide Omnibus
item.description: The Council wants unlimited approvals limited to low-risk substances, while 550 scientists urge suspension and EFSA says about 50 more experts would cut reassessment delays.

item.title: Commission proposes secret 2027 solidarity pool as EU relocations fall short
item.description: EU governments relocated fewer than 9,000 asylum seekers in 2026 against an agreed figure of 21,000, and the Council must now set each country's share by the end of next year.

item.title: Europe earned a seat at the Ukraine talks. One negotiator can take it.
item.description: Moscow set the guest list, and Europe still has no one to send. On 13 November EU leaders must name a single negotiator with a standing mandate, before the next round opens.

item.title: Russian strike on Komyshuvakha kills 43, with 53 still missing
item.description: Rescuers and police died in the attack, which the UN says may have violated international humanitarian law. Talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations are set for Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

item.title: More than 6,000 German troops launch double exercise in Lithuania
item.description: The 10th Panzer Division tests new loitering munitions as Germany's brigade in the country grows toward full strength by the end of 2027.

item.title: Male State denies sending Rome email that threatened two flights
item.description: Threats disrupted airports in Madrid, Prague, Sofia and Brussels on 5 November, and investigators have not yet established who sent them.

item.title: Six Nordic defence firms propose one shared procurement chain
item.description: Ericsson, Kongsberg, Nokia, Patria and Saab launched the Nordic Compass Defence Track in August, and the six firms now pitch joint missile warning, maritime and digital projects to five governments.

item.title: The Netherlands handed its air defence spine to Washington
item.description: Anduril's software now connects the whole counter-drone chain, while the ministry cut its own innovation budget. Urgency can be the reason once. It cannot become the standing excuse.

item.title: Darmanin says a Mélenchon or Le Pen win would 'kill Europe as it exists'
item.description: The French justice minister backed Édouard Philippe for 2027 and called for a Europe of power, not discussion, at a Barcelona event with Spain's foreign minister.

item.title: The veto pen did not change hands. Fund Europe's defence.
item.description: 86 senators voted for sanctions on Russia and one waiver undid them. The Council should stop budgeting around American promises and borrow together to build European defence.

item.title: Eight parliaments wrote one law. Brussels should read it as a mandate
item.description: Eight national drafts against addictive design, written together, are one common mandate from eight democracies. The Commission's fragmentation warning protects delay, and delay is what the platforms want.

item.title: Montenegro is ready. The holdup sits in Brussels, not Podgorica.
item.description: Close the chapters by the end of 2026 and sign the treaty on schedule, so the governments in the Council prove that merit moves at the speed of the willing, not at the speed of the slowest capital.

item.title: EU adds names to Russia sanctions list, bringing total near 4,600
item.description: The newly listed people and companies in Russia's military-industrial complex face asset freezes, and natural persons face travel bans, and turn over at least €20 billion a year. Work on a 22nd sanctions package continues without an adoption date.

item.title: Brussels bought the sovereign cloud. The capitals won't plug it in.
item.description: Europe built an air-gapped cloud that no American kill switch can reach, then Scotland paused approvals and Denmark could put the data centres it needs to the back of the power queue. That has to change now.

item.title: MEPs to debate shielding critical infrastructure from cyber attacks
item.description: The debate builds on a September report naming Russia the EU's primary security threat and follows the Commission's proposed Cybersecurity Act overhaul. The file now sits with the Parliament's industry committee.

item.title: Ukraine-built 290 g receiver turns Russian drone signals into live video
item.description: D·Vision SDR scans from 500 MHz to 8.7 GHz, covering the band Russia's Molniya drones moved to in June. Experts warn a Russian shift to digital video could sideline it.

item.title: Bulgaria elects Iliana Iotova as its first woman president
item.description: The Central Election Commission confirmed her win over Gyurov in the November 1 runoff, with all 15 members voting in favour.

item.title: British and French troops in Ukraine could fire back if attacked, officials say
item.description: The stabilisation force would count more than 10,000 members, run without US technology, including Starlink, and stay away from the front line. No ceasefire is in force yet.

item.title: Let the Sejm's judges sit
item.description: Karol Nawrocki has refused for seven months to swear in four judges elected by Poland's parliament. When one office stalls a constitutional court, Europe is right to say the answer is a working court, not a standoff.

item.title: Ban addictive design EU-wide, not country by country
item.description: Brussels has the evidence, the findings and the law to stop infinite scroll and autoplay. It must decide now, because a patchwork of national bans leaves you unprotected in Lisbon or Tallinn.
